Gastric adenocarcinoma is a low-probability differential diagnosis.
The final diagnosis is gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumor.

clusters.summary: Initial presentation and patient context: chronic LUQ pain with a progressively enlarging palpable upper abdominal mass in a 33-year-old woman.

clusters.label: examination
clusters.summary: Physical exam indicates a fixed deep LUQ mass extending below the costal margin without acute abdomen or systemic illness.

clusters.label: test_ordering
clusters.summary: Imaging and tumor markers show a large well-defined gastric-adjacent mixed solid-cystic lesion with calcifications and no invasion/metastases; CEA and CA19-9 are normal.

clusters.label: differential_generation
clusters.summary: Reasoning narrows the differential away from common adenocarcinomas and toward a slow-growing gastric wall or splenic-bed mesenchymal process, noting absent systemic/GI obstructive features.

clusters.label: differential_generation
clusters.summary: GIST is favored over duplication cyst based on gastric wall attachment, exophytic well-defined mass, mixed solid-cystic change, calcifications, adult age, and progressive palpable mass.

clusters.label: differential_generation

clusters.label: final_decision
clusters.summary: Overall synthesis concludes gastric gastrointestinal stromal tumor as the most likely and final diagnosis, with other differentials ranked lower.
